discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution (BB84 and entanglement-based QKD)

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the laws of quantum physics themselves, through the no-cloning principle and measurement disturbance, can guarantee the secrecy of a shared key. Ekert (1991) independently linked key security to entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities, turning a foundational test of nature into a cryptographic resource and founding the device-independent paradigm. Together these ideas created the field of quantum information science as a physical discipline: they inspired the first single-photon experiments, decades of work on photon sources, detectors and entanglement distribution, and today's fibre, free-space and satellite QKD networks and national quantum communication infrastructures. Their discovery is the clearest example of fundamental quantum physics, superposition, uncertainty and nonlocality, becoming a working technology with a provable security that no classical scheme can offer.
